candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall ensure that the sewage sludge meets the requirements in 40 CFR 258 concerning the quality of the sludge dispose d in a municipal solid waste landfill unit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 40 CFR 258 quality criteria are treated as enforceable numeric limits for sludge disposed in an MSWLF—and which parameters they cover—determines which limit values are applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when external Section 405(d)(2) pollutant criteria supersede or supplement in-permit sludge pollutant limits affects which numeric limits govern FY2025 compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The combined 'once during the life of the permit' and 'within one year from the effective date' timing conditions determine whether TCLP monitoring was required during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required sampling point and timing relative to final treatment and site departure define when TCLP monitoring must occur, affecting whether monitoring was due for any given period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Hazardous-waste classification is a conditional trigger for alternative handling and disposal obligations; interpretation of whether that classification is established changes which monitoring and management requirements apply and how missing TCLP or classification evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as hazardous waste and disposal occurs only at certified facilities affects enforceable disposal restrictions and the monitoring or reporting obligations tied to TCLP failure and unauthorized disposal.

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A failed TCLP triggers a time-bound notification requirement; interpretation of what constitutes test failure and when the 24-hour window starts determines whether this reporting obligation applied.

candidates.exact_span: A written report shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Failed TCLP results impose a follow-on written reporting obligation with a fixed deadline, which is a distinct monitoring/reporting requirement whose applicability depends on interpreting TCLP failure.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested as needed, or at a minimum, once/year in accordance with the method 9095 (Paint Filter Liquids Test) as described in "Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'as needed' qualifier versus the annual minimum frequency determines how often Paint Filter testing was required in FY2025, and whether absence of a result reflects conditional non-requirement, a missing required test, or an unresolved case.

candidates.exact_span: Recordkeeping requirements - The permittee shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Recordkeeping and five-year retention obligations define what evidence should exist for sludge testing and disposal activities, affecting evaluation of whether monitoring was performed and how missing or undocumented results should be classified.
